messages:
maya: Quick sync please — ACME onramp hit us with a hard SLA ask: 95th p95 < 250ms for text-gen and guaranteed dedicated capacity during pilot. Need alignment on scope + sequencing. Who's free to triage?
liam: I can start — can we clarify pilot traffic shape? bursts or steady 50 qps?
maya: Product got pilot profile: ~40 qps steady, 200 qps bursts for <2min during peak. Mostly short prompts (avg 80 tokens).
sofia: Runtime note: bursts are fine if we prewarm. Need PK cache priming and a warm pool; otherwise cold KV refill will blow p95.
raj: Infra constraints: Dedicated pool can be reserved but committed GPUs needed. How long is pilot? monthly or 3mo?
maya: 3 months with possibility to convert to dedicated commit. Customer expects a staging ramp next month.
elaine: Security question: will this customer require BYOK/KMS integration and audit logs? That affects Private vs Hosted decision and timeline.
maya: Yes — legal asked for KMS and audit trail. They prefer VPC peering if possible.
sam: Eng-SRE: we can do a prewarm playbook: replicate a 5-instance warm pool and autoscale thresholds. Suggest canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with performance gates.
liam: What are the gates? propose: p95 <= 250ms, error-rate < 0.5%, token throughput >= baseline. Also monitor cost-per-token so we can flag economics.
sofia: Runtime tuning: quantized variant (int8) hits lower latency but subtle quality delta. Need eval against ACME prompts before swapping in. We can serve quantized as fallback only.
product-ops: Proposal: broker capacity by priority tiers. During pilot, route ACME to a reserved pool; overflow routes to shared pool with strict throttles and graceful degradation to smaller model if needed.
raj: Network/peering ops: VPC peering + stricter egress rules will add 2–3 days infra work once we have IP ranges. Handoff needs an owner.
eliine: (typo) sorry, meant elaine: KMS integration requires security review; estimate 1 sprint if we use our KMS provider flow, 2+ if customer HSM.
maya: @liam @sofia can you scope the eval and prewarm plan? @raj please list infra prerequisites. We need a go/no-go by EOD Friday so sales can lock pilot dates.
liam: I'll have a draft prewarm + canary playbook by tomorrow EOD. Includes autoscale thresholds and `replicas=5, burst_target=200` as a starting point.
sofia: I'll run quality regressions on the quantized family against their sample prompts. ETA 36 hours.
raj: I'll post the IP ranges, peering checklist, and estimated crew-hours (network + infra) in #eng-infra by noon.
elaine: I'll start the security intake form and flag KMS/HSM variance. Also will need compliance contact from the customer.
product-ops: Ops note: we should capture launch acceptance criteria in a tiny ticket: acceptance = (canary p95<=250ms AND stability >= 48h at 25% traffic AND KMS audit events streaming).
maya: Love that — I'll create the ticket and tag owners. One more: fallback model specs? we need a clear downgrade path if cost/latency spikes.
sofia: Suggest fallback to a faster, smaller model variant with explicit prompt templates to maintain quality. I'll draft recommended prompt templates.
sam: I'll add tracing hooks and a temporary synthetic load generator for the canary so we can reproduce bursts.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/ACME-pilot-prewarm -> staging at 2027-05-11T09:00Z (CI green). @deploy-bot triggered by sam. :rocket:
liam: Ok — summary: liam prewarm + playbook; sofia quant eval & fallback prompts; raj infra + peering; elaine security intake; sam tracing + synthetic; maya product ticket + acceptance criteria. Go/no-go EOD Friday.
maya: Thanks all — small follow-up: @product-ops can you own post-mortem template for pilot so we capture perf vs cost?
product-ops: Yup. I'll attach a lightweight postmortem template to the ticket and add checklist items for economics, quality regressions, and SLO drift. :+1:
maya: Great. Closing loop — will update sales and ACME with tentative pilot cadence after EOD review.
liam: 👍
